nodes.intent: Start one pool instance that is safely bound to one configured repository
nodes.change_spec: Add the smallest owner-supplied startup configuration for one pool instance: a canonical local repository root, a permitted base-ref policy resolved to an immutable commit for each execution, allowed changed paths, verification commands, exact model, execution bounds, sandbox/runtime root, one-slot concurrency, and a persistent host-owned review checkout outside Worker containers. Validate and freeze this execution policy before any Worker launch, expose it through a narrow Agent Execution interface, and keep credentials outside the configuration and Worker environment. Reuse the passed generalized runner; this node does not add task intake, HTTP, SQLite work lifecycle, multi-repository routing, GitHub API access, remote push, automatic PR creation, or concurrent execution.
acceptance_criteria: A pool instance starts only from a complete owner-supplied configuration and fails before Worker/model work when the repository root, base-ref policy, allowed paths, commands, model, bounds, runtime root, or persistent host-owned review checkout is malformed, mutable where an immutable value is required, or escapes its permitted filesystem boundary

The configuration binds exactly one canonical repository identity, one-slot runtime policy, and one persistent host-owned review checkout; repository, branch, command, model, path, credential, and execution-bound values cannot be supplied by future task requests

A narrow configuration-derived execution-policy interface supplies the generalized runner with the resolved immutable base commit and fixed repository policy without exposing credentials or invoking a shell outside the existing runner and sandbox paths

Deterministic tests cover valid startup, hostile and incomplete configuration rejection before runner launch, immutable base resolution, independent runtime roots and review checkouts for separately configured pool instances, and rejection of a Worker-container-owned review location

nodes.intent: Submit a task to one configured pool and observe one durable real Worker result
nodes.change_spec: Add the smallest production composition root that connects the existing authenticated POST /tasks adapter and direct-task validation to the repository-bound pool configuration, SQLite work import, a SQLite-backed pending-task claim loop, one ready Minimal Pool Runtime slot, and bounded status queries. The request carries only one caller-authored task and an idempotency key; the configured pool supplies repository identity, resolved base commit, allowed paths, verification commands, model, execution bounds, and sandbox policy. Persist a generated immutable execution snapshot that combines the accepted task with that fixed pool policy, launches the generalized runner, and records terminal status. It must not invoke decomposition, Gate 1, a separate durable queue service, full CRAFTS, Tier-2 grading, GitHub delivery, multi-repository routing, or caller-selected execution policy.
acceptance_criteria: An authenticated task-only POST /tasks request persists one accepted direct task and a generated immutable execution snapshot, returns a stable submission/work identity, and replays the same caller/key/payload to the original identity; repository, branch, commands, paths, model, bounds, and credentials are not request-selectable

A SQLite-backed claim loop dispatches the persisted task through the configured repository-bound pool to one fresh Minimal Pool Runtime Worker and recovers pending work after process restart without Redis or BullMQ

The direct path cannot invoke decomposition or Gate 1, retains gate2_required=true, and exposes bounded caller-owned submission, attempt, and terminal-result status without leaking configuration, credentials, host paths, or raw Worker output
A service-level test submits one approved task to a configured local repository pool and observes its runner-owned terminal result without manual ledger edits or GitHub credentials

nodes.intent: Independently verify arbitrary configured-pool task results
nodes.change_spec: Generalize the fixture verifier into a runner-owned deterministic verifier driven only by the immutable execution snapshot and stored attempt identity. Verify process success, base/result commit relationship, allowed paths, clean repository state, pool-configured verification commands, and result uniqueness, then persist a structured pass/fail result with bounded evidence. Do not add model judging, CRAFTS phase grading, empirical thresholds, transcript object storage, or integration re-verification.
acceptance_criteria: A result passes only when the launched Worker identity matches, the expected commit descends from the snapshot's pinned base, changed paths are allowed, the tree is clean, and every configured verification command succeeds
Worker prose cannot override a failed command, wrong commit, dirty tree, out-of-scope path, duplicate conflicting result, timeout, or missing evidence
The verifier emits and persists one bounded structured verdict linked to submission, work, node, attempt, result, execution snapshot, base commit, and result commit identities
Deterministic tests cover pass, command failure, identity mismatch, commit mismatch, path violation, dirty tree, timeout, and conflicting-result outcomes

nodes.intent: Expose a verified task as a human-reviewable branch and PR-ready artifact
nodes.change_spec: For a deterministically passed configured-pool task, preserve its verified commit on a named local review branch in the configured persistent host-owned review checkout and emit a PR-ready markdown/JSON artifact there. The artifact contains intent, acceptance criteria, changed files, verification commands, verdict, and stable identities. A human can inspect the branch and artifact from the host, then manually push/open the PR. Failed tasks expose bounded failure context and never produce a mergeable review branch. GitHub credentials, automatic PR creation, webhooks, connected-component assembly, comment continuation, and cryptographic Gate 2 records remain deferred.
acceptance_criteria: A passed task produces one local review branch pointing at the independently verified commit in the configured persistent host-owned review checkout and one bounded PR-ready artifact with traversable evidence identities and a branch/artifact locator relative to that checkout

A failed, timed-out, dirty, conflicting, or unverifiable task produces no mergeable review branch and exposes bounded failure context through status; review output never depends on entering a Worker container
Branch and artifact creation are idempotent for the same accepted result and reject conflicting replays

An end-to-end test covers authenticated task submission through configured-pool fresh Worker execution, deterministic verification, host-accessible local review branch creation, and human-readable output without GitHub credentials
